points.en: grey median crown bordered by dark lateral crown stripes

art.subject: Grey-crowned Warbler (Phylloscopus tephrocephalus), adult (sexes alike, plumage similar year-round): crown and nape grey, bordered on each side by a black lateral crown stripe running from the forehead to the nape; a complete, bright golden-yellow eye-ring; cheeks yellowish-green; upperparts bright olive-green; wings and tail olive-green with darker centres, usually without a wing-bar; entire underparts bright yellow; outer tail feathers with white on the inner webs; bill with a dusky upper mandible and pale orange lower mandible; dark eye; pale orange-yellow legs.
art.pose: perched on a thin twig in the mid-canopy, side view, alert
art.scene: deciduous woodland on a Korean offshore island in May with fresh green leaves and dappled light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched on a thin twig: round head with a bright grey median crown stripe bordered by dark lateral crown stripes reaching almost to the bill, yellow eye-ring, short thin bill with a pale lower mandible, olive-green upperparts and wings with at most a faint wing-bar, saturated yellow underparts, pale legs
adult, three-quarter front view perched: grey crown with dark lateral crown stripes, yellow eye-ring, saturated yellow throat, breast and belly, olive-green wings without a clear wing-bar
art.build: A small, compact, round-headed warbler, smaller than a sparrow and about the size of a Japanese White-eye, with a fairly broad, flat-based bill and noticeable bristles at the gape. Bill shorter than the head. Legs slender and pale. Wings short and rounded. Tail medium and square-ended, often flicked open to show white in the outer feathers. Very active, making short sallies for insects in the lower and middle canopy.
avoid: Do not paint a green crown centre; that is Green-crowned Warbler (Phylloscopus burkii).
Do not paint obvious pale wing-bars (Bianchi's or Martens's Warbler).
Do not break the eye-ring; it is a complete yellow ring.
Do not add a supercilium or a dark eye-stripe; the face shows only the yellow eye-ring below the black crown stripes.
